description: We’re a team from Hyderabad building for Flame in Freefall: AI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data. Our plan is an interactive dashboard that pulls together NASA’s microgravity combustion findings, ranks them by relevance to spacecraft fire safety, and explains each result with links back to its source. We’re building it in Python (Streamlit) with a retrieval-based approach, so the insights stay traceable instead of invented.
summary: Astraeon turns 24 NASA microgravity combustion investigations into a searchable fire-safety dashboard for spacecraft and Moon bases. It ranks each experiment by how directly it applies to four settings: spacecraft, space station, Moon base and rover. It also maps 746 real flight tests against Moon-base air, and answers questions with cited sources. Its key finding: only one experiment, ACME CFI-G, has burned flames at test-by-test Moon-base conditions. No solid cabin material has been tested there, and no experiment has run in lunar gravity.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Astraeon helps mission planners, students and researchers see what NASA's fire experiments actually tell us about fire on future Moon bases, and what they don't. It has eight pages:

- Home: the key findings at a glance.

- Experiments: search and filter all 24 PSI combustion investigations by topic, fuel, oxygen level and Moon evidence.

- Rank: a 0-10 relevance score for spacecraft, space station, Moon base and rover, with the reason behind every score.

- Compare: up to three experiments side by side.

- Moon-base explorer: set oxygen and pressure, or pick a planned habitat atmosphere, and see which real flight tests ran nearby.

- Fire history: Apollo 1, Apollo 13 and the Mir fire, plus open research gaps.

- Ask Astraeon: a question-answering assistant that searches only our checked data and cites numbered sources.

- About: data sources, evidence rules, AI use and team.

WHAT WE FOUND

- Only ACME CFI-G has test-by-test records inside the Moon-base zone: 17 hot flames at 33-39% oxygen and 7.35 psi, using gas fuels on a burner, not cabin materials.

- FLEX is a near miss: 17 droplet tests at 30-34% oxygen ran at 10.3-10.5 psi.

- ACME BRE and FLEX-2 are unconfirmed, because PSI doesn't record which pressure went with which test.

- No solid cabin material has been fire-tested at Moon-base air in this dataset, and no experiment ran in lunar or Martian partial gravity. These are the gaps future research should close.

HOW WE BUILT IT

Python and Streamlit, using data from NASA PSI (psi.nasa.gov). We checked oxygen and pressure values against each investigation's experimental tables. A blank value means the source doesn't report it, never zero. Ask Astraeon uses BM25 search over our data, and Google Gemini writes the answer with numbered citations.

EVIDENCE RULE

A match on oxygen and pressure is not a safety verdict. Astraeon shows where evidence exists and where it doesn't, so "untested" is never mistaken for "safe."

USE OF AI

Claude drafted the plain-English summaries and glossary from the data rows. A script checked every one against its source, and a team member then read it. Claude Code wrote most of the dashboard code with us. We chose the design and the evidence rules, reviewed the output and tested every page. Gemini phrases Ask Astraeon answers from our checked data only.

TEAM

Maimuna Afrah (lead): data, dashboard, Ask Astraeon, final rankings

Ishrat Siddiqui: AI summaries, glossary, incident history, research gaps, deployment, submission

Madeeha Khan: original relevance rankings
